name: Order-flow imbalance
economic_mechanism: Net aggressive demand relative to available liquidity moves price
observable_signature: Signed aggressive volume minus available liquidity at the touch
strongest_support: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov: robust short-horizon OFI/price relation in 50 U.S. equities (SRC-0102)
strongest_counterargument: Current venue-specific net edge and decay are unknown; the equity sample does not transfer to CME/Eurex/crypto

name: Queue imbalance / depletion
economic_mechanism: One side's displayed queue is more vulnerable than the other
structural_driver: Bid/ask queue-size asymmetry and depletion rate
strongest_support: Gould & Bonart 2015: next-mid-price direction predictable for ten liquid Nasdaq names, especially large-tick (SRC-0101)
strongest_counterargument: 2015 sample, gross/predictive only; execution cost and latency may consume it

name: Microprice
economic_mechanism: An imbalance-adjusted estimator of fair price
strongest_support: Stoikov 2018: microprice improves on midpoint by incorporating imbalance (SRC-0104)
strongest_counterargument: A better estimator is not executable alpha

name: Liquidity replenishment failure
economic_mechanism: The book fails to refill after aggressive flow
observable_signature: Depth recovery half-time after a depletion event
strongest_counterargument: No current direct replication locked

name: Adverse-selection avoidance
economic_mechanism: Value comes from not providing liquidity when informed/urgent flow arrives
observable_signature: Markout distribution conditional on own fill
strongest_counterargument: Requires real or simulated fills, not forecasts; unmeasured in this evidence lock

name: Spread capture
economic_mechanism: A passive trader earns spread/rebate for warehousing inventory and liquidity risk
observable_signature: Passive fill events with post-fill price path
strongest_counterargument: Queue position and adverse selection can reverse gross spread

name: Inventory effects
economic_mechanism: Dealer/market-maker inventory creates temporary price pressure
structural_driver: Price response conditional on inferred inventory
strongest_counterargument: Inventory is usually latent and not observable in this evidence lock

name: Volatility transitions
economic_mechanism: Regime shifts alter conditional edge and execution cost
structural_driver: Book thinning, trade intensity, realized volatility
strongest_counterargument: Regime classification can lag and costs rise precisely in transitions

name: Forced liquidation cascades
economic_mechanism: Leveraged positions are mechanically closed
structural_driver: Liquidation events, rapid directional flow, leverage state
strongest_counterargument: Needs market-wide point-in-time liquidation data and after-cost decay evidence
report_evidence_status: Mechanically plausible; direct edge evidence UNKNOWN

name: Stop cascades
economic_mechanism: Price triggers clustered conditional market orders
observable_signature: Flow bursts at salient price levels
strongest_counterargument: Stop inventory is often unobservable ex ante

name: Funding / basis dislocation
economic_mechanism: Position demand creates a carry wedge between venues or instruments
structural_driver: Funding rates, futures basis, borrow and carry
strongest_counterargument: Capital, funding, borrow and regime risk matter; not locked here

name: Calendar roll effects
economic_mechanism: Mandated migration between expiries creates predictable flow
structural_driver: Spread volume/open-interest migration around the roll
strongest_counterargument: Highly visible and professionally arbitraged

name: Index / rebalance flows
economic_mechanism: Funds must trade to benchmark composition or weight changes
structural_driver: Published changes plus closing flow and auction imbalance
observable_signature: Published index changes with closing-auction flow
strongest_counterargument: Anticipation/crowding may transfer gains to earlier participants

name: Auction imbalances
economic_mechanism: Benchmark/close demand is concentrated into a clearing event
observable_signature: Published indicative price and imbalance side/size
strongest_support: Nasdaq NOII makes auction imbalance publicly observable (SRC-0108)
strongest_counterargument: Observability does not establish excess return after auction impact, and it is observable to everyone

name: Cross-venue lead-lag
economic_mechanism: One venue discovers price before another
structural_driver: Conditional lag after a source-venue move
strongest_counterargument: Likely highly latency-sensitive; stale quotes may vanish before fill

name: Fragmented stale pricing
economic_mechanism: Routing/fragmentation leaves temporary price discrepancies
strongest_counterargument: The most obvious forms invite dedicated low-latency competition

name: Options surface relative value
economic_mechanism: Relative mispricing across strikes and expiries
strongest_counterargument: Model risk, spreads, legging, vol/spot hedging and fee complexity

name: Dealer hedging / gamma effects
economic_mechanism: Option inventory can induce predictable hedging demand
structural_driver: Spot flow conditional on option positioning
strongest_counterargument: Dealer positioning is imperfectly observed; causal attribution is difficult

name: Volatility risk premium
economic_mechanism: Investors pay to transfer crash/variance risk
strongest_counterargument: Not adequately audited for this M1 tuple; the premium is compensation for tail risk, not necessarily alpha

name: Fee / rebate effects
economic_mechanism: Venue incentives change optimal provision and routing behaviour
economic_payer: Venue and participants via the fee schedule
structural_driver: Fill economics conditional on fee code
strongest_support: Cboe BZX rebate/remove schedule is explicit; Coinbase and Kraken tiers are explicit (SRC-0114, SRC-0105, SRC-0106)
strongest_counterargument: Rebate harvesting without adverse-selection modelling is invalid
report_evidence_status: CONSENSUS FACT that incentives differ materially

name: Market-design quirks
economic_mechanism: Rules create localized flow/priority effects
strongest_support: Venue heterogeneity is documented (matching processes, fee codes, interfaces)
strongest_counterargument: Must be evaluated one rule and one venue at a time; a generic rule model is unjustified

name: Event/news latency
economic_mechanism: Public information is incorporated at different speeds
strongest_counterargument: Lowest-latency versions are infrastructure-dominated; semantic value must beat faster baselines

name: Behavioural flow
economic_mechanism: Recurrent human/institutional behaviour creates conditional demand
strongest_counterargument: Easy to overfit calendar patterns

name: Horizon mismatch
economic_mechanism: Large institutions cannot optimize tiny-capacity opportunities
strongest_counterargument: Must demonstrate the opportunity is too small or operationally unattractive to larger firms

name: Balance-sheet-constrained liquidity provision
economic_mechanism: Capital and risk limits make compensation for warehousing risk persistent
structural_driver: Spreads/basis widening when balance sheet is scarce
observable_signature: Spread and basis levels versus balance-sheet proxies
strongest_counterargument: Empirical lock incomplete; often earns a risk premium rather than pure alpha
